question:
Observe the given figure and answer question below:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/32cc014796569b1b8ae9c10b0b338953fbc2c7520f401c05c884f703c6e19363.png] 

If 50 play football, 40 play cricket and 30 play basketball, then what is the number of players who play football or cricket but not basketball?
solution:
The shaded part represents is the number of players who play football or cricket but not basketball.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2875e1c328f90aca11925084c6357ff3b992563791e25107103876036b2fbb90.png] 

 n(A∪B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A⋂B)

The number of players who play football or cricket but NOT basketball = Number of player who play cricket and football – (Number of player who play both basketball and cricket + Number of player who play both Basketball and football + Number of player who play Basketball, Cricket and football)

And

Number of player who play cricket and football = The number of players who play football + The number of players who play cricket - The number of players who play both football and cricket

Number of player who play cricket and football = 50 + 40 - (14 + 5) = 71

So,

The number of players who play football or cricket but not basketball =

= 71 – (9 + 7 + 5)

= 71 – 21

= 50

Hence, ‘**50’** number of players who play football or cricket but NOT basketball.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Players who play** only Football = 50 - (14 + 7 + 5) = 24**

Players who play only Cricket= 40 - (14 + 9 + 5) = 12

Players who play only Basketball = 30 - (9 + 7 + 5) = 9
